verdict.rationale: Warp documents its own privacy controls: telemetry opt-out, a native Network Log for watching outbound telemetry, unconditional secret redaction, and zero data retention on Business/Enterprise plans. Hands-on users report turning AI features off, and the co-founder states the login requirement was removed. However, Free-plan users must keep telemetry enabled to use AI, AI features still require login, and users report that proactive AI features sent terminal data by default without explicit consent. That weakens the 'clear control' part of the story. Missing for 10: AI use without login or telemetry on the Free plan, opt-in (rather than default-on) consent for proactive AI data sharing, first-party documentation of a single switch that fully disables AI.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use or fully disable AI features with clear control over what session data leaves my machine, without a forced login

citations.quote: Monitor telemetry in real-time with Warp’s native Network Log. Opt out of telemetry at any time
Telemetry must be enabled to use AI features on the Free plan, while paid plans can opt out at any time and continue using Warp, including AI.
Warp unconditionally applies Secret Redaction in all AI interactions to ensure that any sensitive data is _never_ collected or sent to third parties.
Business and Enterprise plans are covered by our Zero Data Retention (ZDR) agreement. No AI interaction or console data is ever collected.
Warp co-founder: fair criticism, and this is the reason we removed the login requirement
